title: Windows Node MXC sandbox — whoami fails with 0xC0000142
subtitle: openclaw/openclaw-windows-node #1764
author: jadus1210-crypto
body:
Environment

OpenClaw Windows Companion: 2026.10.4-alpha.6

OpenClaw Gateway: 2026.10.4

Windows 11 Home, build 26200

AMD Ryzen 7 5700X, 32 GB RAM

Gateway: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04

Windows Node: connected and paired

Steps to reproduce

Keep the MXC sandbox enabled.

Execute whoami using exec with host=node.

Do not supply custom environment variables.

Actual result

(Command exited with code -1073741502)

Exit code: 0xC0000142 (STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED).

MXC diagnostics

tier: base-container

needsDaclAugmentation: false

isolationSessionAvailable: true

warnings: []

envKeys: []

allowWindowsUi: false

containment: mxc

Execution is approved, but the process exits without stdout or stderr.

Additional findings

The Gateway and Windows Node remain connected.

No reparse points were detected in the examined OpenClawTray directories.

No matching events were found in the Windows Application or CodeIntegrity logs using the tested filters.

Previous version 2026.9.8-1 failed with CreateProcessSecurityEnvironment / 0x800701C0.

Expected result

The sandboxed command whoami should execute successfully without disabling MXC.

Question

Is this a known MXC AppContainer issue on Windows 11 build 26200? Is there a supported fix that preserves sandbox isolation?

comments.author: jadus1210-crypto
comments.body:
**Compatibility test result — SUCCESS**

I tested the existing **Allow Windows UI APIs** compatibility setting on the affected Windows 11 host.

- OpenClaw Companion: `2026.10.4-alpha.6`
- MXC sandbox: enabled
- Windows UI APIs: enabled through the Sandbox UI
- Command: `whoami` via `exec`, `host=node`
- No custom environment variables

**Result:**
```text
nick12\jadus
Exit code: 0
```

Previously, the same command failed with `0xC0000142` when Windows UI APIs were disabled.

This strongly supports Win32k denial as the cause of the failure.

The command response did not include MXC logs confirming `allowWindowsUi=True`. The compatibility setting was visibly enabled in the Windows Companion UI.

The next step is to confirm the effective sandbox policy in sanitized logs and clarify the security trade-off of leaving this compatibility option enabled.

comments.author: roboclaw-bot
comments.body:
Closing the original Win32k-denial case as obsolete on current main. The affected-host follow-up confirmed that the same whoami command succeeds with MXC still enabled when Windows UI API compatibility is enabled. #1726 (feat: upgrade Windows node sandboxing to MXC 1.0 .NET SDK) subsequently made that compatibility policy fixed and retired the old toggle; current code and regression tests keep container isolation and input-injection restrictions. This does not claim that every 0xC0000142 cause is solved. If it recurs on a build containing that change, please reopen with the exact version and sanitized effective-containment result, without disabling MXC.

Affected-host confirmation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1764#issuecomment-6258607388
